provenance: PR #29 R24, T-R34. `published-band-matches-the-ledger` grades `rule(published) == rule(ledger max)` and not `published >= ledger max`, so a published maximum that is below the ledger's is green as long as both derive the same ceiling. R24 asked whether that was a decision or an artefact of what was convenient to grade. It is a decision (ADR-019 §6) and this case is what makes it one: it drives the same pure judgement with a synthetic ledger, asserts the miss IS green up to the top of the band and red one hundredth of a second past it, asserts the harmful direction (a published maximum that justifies a LOWER ceiling than the truth -- R21's 12.96s published against 13.57s recorded) is red on the same property, and asserts ADR-019 publishes the size of the hole as a number derived from the rule's own constants (5s of ceiling / 1.15 = 4.35s of wall clock) rather than a sentence someone can quietly soften. Delete the declaration and this goes red; tighten the property and this goes red; leave both alone and the reader is told exactly what the grader does not see. PR #35 R1 then found the declaration was published three times and graded once: `_BAND_SLACK_LINE` matched one sentence in ADR-019, while README and §6's own restatement carried the same figure unread — so amending the rule and repairing the graded sentence left two documents publishing 4.35s against a real bound of 8.7s, green. Every restatement now carries the marker `one ceiling step (**N.NNs**)` and every match in BOTH documents is graded against `_band_step_s`. PR #35 R10: the round-2 repair added the fourth copy in the same commit that claimed every copy was graded -- an unmarked `4.35s` in §6's own rewrite. The marker closed the instance, not the class, so the check now also sweeps both documents for bare occurrences of the current value and requires every one of them to sit inside a marker.

triage.note: tagged invariant, pure code, no network. It pins a KNOWN and BOUNDED miss rather than a defect, which is the only honest way to keep a weak property: the strict form reddens on run-to-run variance, and since every gate run appends to the ledger it would redden the NEXT commit rather than the one that got slower. The bound is the thing that makes the weak form safe -- a published maximum can never be more than one ceiling step low, and the ceiling itself is graded against the ledger directly, so the slack costs the reader precision and never costs the gate its teeth.
triage.watched_red: two rounds, both observed. (1) Case written before the check existed, `--suite invariant` 49/52 = 0.942: [FAIL] published-band-slack-is-declared -- "unknown invariant check published-band-slack", alongside the two reds adding a case always causes -- published-band {suite: fast, published_case_count: 132, actual: 133} + {suite: invariant, published_case_count: 51, actual: 52}, and docs-numbers-are-derived {readme_does_not_say: 'offline gate: 133 cases, zero paid calls'}. (2) Check implemented, ADR-019 not yet amended: wrong [{adr_declares_no_slack: true, one_ceiling_step_is: 4.35}], got {declared_slack_s: 4.35, headroom_s: {fast: 3.23, invariant: 3.27}} -- the mechanical half already green (the miss IS accepted up to the top of the band, red one hundredth past it, R21's direction red) while nothing in the repo told a reader the hole was there, which is precisely the state R24 objected to. Green only once ADR-019 §6 published the bound. Both directions were then re-watched by hand: rewriting §6's number to 4.30s gives {adr_declared_slack: 4.3, one_ceiling_step_is: 4.35}, and deleting the sentence returns it to adr_declares_no_slack. And the property itself was mutated both ways with the case watching: replacing `_band_wrong`'s judgement with the strict `published >= ledger max` gives [{suite: fast, declared_miss_went_red_at: 69.56}, {suite: invariant, declared_miss_went_red_at: 17.39}]; removing the judgement entirely gives [{suite: fast, stayed_green_past_the_band_at: 69.57, derives: 85, published_derives: 80}, {suite: invariant, stayed_green_past_the_band_at: 17.4, derives: 25, published_derives: 20}, {r21_underpublished_band_went_green: [12.96, 13.57]}]. So the case is red if the decision is silently tightened and red if it is silently abandoned. Note the two headroom figures quoted above (fast 3.23, invariant 3.27) are the ones measured against the bands ADR-019 published BEFORE this commit (66.33s at 132 cases, 14.12s at 51); the republished bands (66.38s at 133, 13.22s at 52) give 3.18 and 4.17, and `got.headroom_s` is recomputed from the doc on every run rather than stored. Cold review then added two more mutations, both watched: amending ADR-013's rounding step from 5 to 10 with the docs untouched gives [{adr_declared_slack: 4.35, one_ceiling_step_is: 8.7}, {r21_underpublished_band_green_on_property_2: [12.96, 13.57]}] -- the second entry is the point, since under a coarser rounding R21's own defect stops being visible to property 2 at all, which is why `_band_step_s` reads the step off `_band_rule` instead of re-typing 5/1.15. PR #35 R1, watched twice: editing README's copy alone to 8.70s gives [{readme: declares_wrong_slack, declared: 8.7, one_ceiling_step_is: 4.35}] -- under the old regex that edit was invisible. And the reviewer's own scenario, amending ADR-013's rounding step 5->10 and repairing only ONE of the ADR's sentences, gives [{adr: declares_wrong_slack, declared: 4.35, one_ceiling_step_is: 8.7}, {readme: declares_wrong_slack, declared: 4.35, one_ceiling_step_is: 8.7}, {r21_underpublished_band_green_on_property_2: [12.96, 13.57]}] -- the unrepaired copies now name themselves. PR #35 R10, the reviewer's own two mutations against the unmarked copy: rewriting it to `99.99s` inside the marker gives [{adr: declares_wrong_slack, declared: 99.99, one_ceiling_step_is: 4.35}], and leaving it bare as "once per 4.35s" gives [{adr: unmarked_copies_of_the_slack_scalar, loose: 1, marked: 1, value: 4.35}] -- which is exactly the state 4e7120d shipped.
